record19.provenance_conflict: User described remeasurement, but ADC counts match an earlier synthetic-labelled revision; the archived firmware export differs. No independent acquisition verification.

methods.normalization: Unadjusted retained series are divided by their own first retained reading. Correlation is unchanged by this positive scaling. Control contrasts are not divided again.
methods.control_sensitivity: Hardware VUAA1/Fstart minus medium/Fstart; wetlab VUAA1/Fstart minus DMSO/Fstart, each using its own original acquisition start. Fixed native five-point and omitted-first four-point cases. F0 endpoint corrections are constants and cannot change Pearson or Spearman correlation. Medium is a separate pre-addition series; DMSO is a separate well, not a matched hardware vehicle-addition control.
methods.pearson: Mean-centered dot product divided by centered Euclidean norms.
methods.spearman: Pearson correlation of average ranks, exact ties retained.
methods.first_difference: Successive changes on the same fixed, equally spaced comparison grid.
methods.detrended: Residuals after independent ordinary least-squares intercept+slope removal against the same fixed time grid.
methods.interpolation: Piecewise linear on shared support only. No extrapolation, smoothing, lag optimization or time warping.
methods.statistical_scope: Descriptive serial time-point correlations. No independent biological replication, p-values or confidence intervals. Five aligned points do not equal five independent samples.

limits: Nominal hardware6s intervals differ from actual device intervals; the selected replacement has no verified acquisition timestamp.
Both clocks start at their first reading, not a known addition time. Addition-to-first-read delays are unknown.
Shared monotonic recovery can correlate across mismatched constructs. The all-pair matrix tests this descriptive specificity question.
Hardware measures mixed electrical channel amplitudes; wetlab measures RFU in separate wells. No gain, dye-calibration, matrix inverse, F0/DMSO subtraction or concentration conversion is transferred.
Normalization does not correct handling or dilution, and agreement does not establish receptor activity.
